subject: AcmeHealth pilot — temporary pricing carveout for quant pipeline delay
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot timeline: quant rollout implication

Hi Rachel,

Quick note from the pilot team — thanks again for the support last week. We dug into the inference numbers this morning and the missing quantized model path for the new <quant-pipeline> is materially increasing per-token cost for our warm workload. Our engineers estimate a ~2.2x token spend increase on the pilot compared to the plan you and I discussed in July.

This puts the Acme pilot economics off-plan for our board review next week. We need a short-term commercial accommodation while Redwood ships the quant runtime change (team says ~4–6 weeks). Specifically, would Redwood consider a temporary overage discount or credit to hold the pilot economics steady through the rollout?

We can share the detailed cost delta (attached) and are flexible on structure (one-time credit vs. temporary percent off overages). Appreciate any quick guidance — we need something to present in the board packet by next Wednesday.

Attachments: acme_quant_impact_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Emily Park
Director, Cloud Integrations
AcmeHealth

--
On an aside, Tom and I are happy to jump on a 20–30 minute call if it helps crystallize terms.

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot timeline: quant rollout implication

Emily — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachment. I pulled Karthik (CS lead) and Laura (VP Sales) in so we can move quickly. We understand the board timeline and the need to preserve pilot economics while the runtime change lands.

High level response: Redwood is willing to propose a short-term commercial accommodation tied to the quant rollout window, subject to simple guardrails so this doesn't become an open-ended precedent.

Can you confirm: 1) the expected additional spend for the pilot period (total $) vs. the planned commit, and 2) whether you prefer a one-time lump-sum credit or a time-bound percent-off for overages? If you can send the delta spreadsheet as a short summary (highlighted rows), we can fast-track internal approval.

I'll circulate an internal recommended approach by EOD so Laura can sign off if it looks reasonable. If helpful, we can put an offer to paper (term doc) and route it for exec sign-off.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: AcmeHealth quant delta — recommended carveout (for Rachel to offer)

Team — looping you in with an internal recommendation after reviewing Emily's spreadsheet. Key facts:
- Pilot delta: ~$42k additional token spend estimated over the 6-week window.
- Root cause: feature parity (quantized inference path) scheduled for the runtime release in ~4–6 weeks; customer ramp cannot wait.

Recommendation (fast, low-friction):
1) Temporary overage credit equal to 80% of the delta above their committed spend for the pilot period (applies only to the specific model variant used in the pilot).
2) Term length: 60 days from agreement execution.
3) Condition: credit expires on delivery of quantized runtime OR 60 days, whichever comes first.
4) One-pager term doc (no change to underlying MSA); customer signs to acknowledge scope and end date.

Rationale: preserves pilot economics, limits public precedent (scoped to model variant + time box), and is easier for billing to process as a one-time credit. Finance note: this is a non-recurring credit; impact is modest and contained to the Acme deal.

Marcus — if you can confirm finance is comfortable with the one-time credit approach at ~80% of delta we can tee this up for Laura sign-off. If Laura is good with the structure, Rachel can send the terms to Emily and request counter-signature.

-Karthik
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot timeline: quant rollout implication — proposed terms

Emily / Tom — thanks for your patience while we reviewed this internally. Laura approved the one-time credit structure and Marcus confirmed finance is comfortable with the approach. Below are the terms we can offer; if this looks good I will send a short term doc for signature and billing will queue the credit upon execution.

Proposed accommodation (Redwood):
- Amount: one-time credit equal to 80% of the documented delta for the pilot period (per the spreadsheet).
- Scope: applies only to the model variant used in the pilot and to usage during the agreed pilot window.
- Term: credit is valid for 60 days from the execution date or until the quantized runtime is available for the pilot, whichever happens first.
- No change to MSA; one-page acceptance to be signed by Acme.

Attachments: proposed_carveout_terms.docx (term doc draft)

Next steps:
1) Reply with confirmation (one-line) that Acme accepts the term structure.
2) I will send the short term doc for signature and route to billing.
3) Once executed, we will apply the credit within one billing cycle.

We can also jump on a 15-minute call if you want to walk through the wording before signing. Appreciate you raising this early — should keep the board conversation on track.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
